newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to review privatisation after court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Manila to review privatisation after court ruling.

text.p: The Philippines will review its assets set for privatisation because of the Supreme Court ruling overturning the sale of the Manila Hotel, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday.

"We will probably have to look at how the Supreme Court defined items of national patrimony in its decision," de Ocampo told reporters. "Based on this definition, we will start identifying what is and what is not to be privatised."

Earlier on Monday, the Supreme Court said it was overturning the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to Malaysia's Renong Berhad and awarding the contract to the local Manila Prince Hotel Corp because of a "Filipino First" policy.
The ruling was in response to a petition by Prince, which said the Manila Hotel was a national treasure and should not be sold to a foreign entity.

De Ocampo said few state assets would fall into the category of the Manila Hotel but added that all other assets scheduled for privatisation would now be evaluated along the lines suggested by the Supreme Court.
